title: Staged Output & Tool Adaptor PRD (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is an early PRD sketch for a staged-output pattern and a lightweight tool adaptor surface for the Hosted API. The goal: provide developers with predictable, typed incremental responses (partial results + structured tool invocations) while keeping client SDKs ergonomic for low-latency and lossy networks.

Context / motivation:
- Many customers want partial results early (search-like hits, draft paragraphs) while the model continues synthesis and possibly calls external tools (code runner, db lookups, calculators).
- Current streaming surfaces return plain token streams or event frames; tooling and structured outputs are brittle to truncation/network loss and hard to reconcile in client UIs.
- SDKs repeatedly reimplement buffering, resume, and validation logic. We should provide a composable server-side contract to simplify client SDKs and reduce app-level correctness bugs.

Problem statement (specific pain points):
- Tool call handshake is implicit; clients must parse free text to detect tool-frames leading to fragile logic.
- Partial structured outputs (json blobs) are frequently truncated mid-emit and clients struggle to recover typed objects.
- Mobile/edge clients face bandwidth/backpressure tradeoffs; current streaming doesn't allow adaptive fidelity (e.g., brief summary first, then full structured result).
- Observability for partially emitted tool calls is weak: hard to map token-level telemetry to higher-level tool boundaries for billing/SLOs.

Goals:
1) Define a minimal staged-output frame envelope that can carry: incremental human-readable text, typed structural updates (JSON fragments), and tool invocation intents (typed tokenizable descriptors) in the same stream.
2) Expose a thin, deterministic tool adaptor contract (idempotent begin/commit/abort frames) so SDKs can present tool-invocation lifecycle to apps with clear resume behavior.
3) Provide SDK ergonomics: client buffering with configurable durability, resumable snapshots, and adaptive fidelity modes (summary-first, payload-then-metadata).
4) Improve telemetry labels for per-frame latency/cost attribution (map frames to tool ids, model variant, and token counts).

Non-goals:
- Not attempting to replace existing structured-only APIs (e.g., synchronous schema outputs) — this is focused on hybrid streaming + tool flows.
- Not introducing heavy wire-format dependencies (we must stay compatible with existing JSONL/event-stream transports).

Proposed surface (high level):
- Stream-frame envelope (JSON-lines event stream) with the following type union: 
  - {"frame_type":"text_chunk","seq":int,"payload":string} -- human-readable incremental text
  - {"frame_type":"struct_patch","seq":int,"path":string,"patch":string} -- small typed fragment to be applied to a JSON object in client
  - {"frame_type":"tool_begin","seq":int,"tool_id":string,"meta":{...}} -- declarative tool intent, server can pause main generation and await tool resolution
  - {"frame_type":"tool_result","seq":int,"tool_id":string,"result":string,"status":"ok|partial|error"} -- result emission from tool, may stream as multiple frames
  - {"frame_type":"commit","seq":int,"target":string} -- commit semantics for previously emitted partial patches (optional)

Notes:
- seq is monotonic per-stream; clients can detect gaps and request resume tokens.
- path in struct_patch follows a simple JSON-Pointer like syntax for incremental patch application (client-friendly).
- meta must be small; for larger payloads we provide a reference URI that is detachable.

SDK ergonomics (client behavior recommendations):
- SDK default: immediate-replay of text_chunk to consumer UI; buffer struct_patch until commit or explicit apply threshold (size/time). This reduces spurious invalid JSON in UI.
- Durable mode: store last N frames as resume snapshot in SDK; on reconnect send resume_token to server to request missing seq ranges.
- Backpressure API: client exposes a window size (max_outstanding_frames) to server; server will try to avoid emitting more frames than window but may degrade fidelity (send summary frame) if window closes.
- Tool lifecycle mapping in SDK: tool_begin -> SDK emits tool invocation UI with provisional state; tool_result frames arrive and update UI progressively; commit finalizes. Tool aborts/errors are surfaced as structured events.

Server-side semantics and guarantees:
- Best-effort delivery for streaming frames. Frames are ordered by seq. On reconnection with resume_token, server will attempt to resend missing frames up to retention window.
- Idempotency: tool_begin frames carry a client-supplied optional client_op_id to deduplicate cross-reconnect invocation.
- Partial tool results allowed; server may emit status=partial multiple times and eventually status=ok or status=error.
- Commit frames signal that a set of struct_patches should be applied atomically by client; server will emit commit once it believes patch set is complete.

Observability and billing implications:
- Each frame has a token_count and estimated_compute label (added to meta) so we can attribute cost early.
- New trace spans: frame_emit, tool_invoke, tool_resolve, commit_apply. These will let Console show per-frame latency/cost.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Existing token streams remain supported. We will offer staged-output as an opt-in MIME/profile header (e.g., Accept: application/x-rw-staged+jsonl).
- If client doesn't understand staged frames, server can emit a fallback text-only stream (text_chunk concatenation) to preserve UX.

API examples (pseudo JSON-lines):
1) Start:
{"frame_type":"text_chunk","seq":1,"payload":"Searching similar docs..."}
{"frame_type":"tool_begin","seq":2,"tool_id":"search_v1","meta":"{"query":"invoice 2024"}","client_op_id":"op-123"}
2) Tool results stream:
{"frame_type":"tool_result","seq":3,"tool_id":"search_v1","result":"[{\"id\":1,\"title\":\"Invoice Q1\"}]","status":"partial"}
{"frame_type":"tool_result","seq":4,"tool_id":"search_v1","result":"[{\"id\":1,\"title\":\"Invoice Q1\"}]","status":"ok"}
3) Structural patch + commit:
{"frame_type":"struct_patch","seq":5,"path":"/results/0/summary","patch":"Draft: found an invoice from Jan 2024"}
{"frame_type":"commit","seq":6,"target":"/results"}

Operational rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (Experiment): internal-only SDK + Console experiment, 2 weeks. Ship server-side experimental flag and SDK opt-in.
- Phase 1 (Beta): selective customer alpha (help & solutions), telemetry enabled, 6 weeks.
- Phase 2 (GA): public API, stable retention/resume SLAs, docs and migration guide, 8–10 weeks after Beta.

Acceptance criteria (for Beta):
- SDK can resume streams across transient network disconnects for up to 30s retention with consistent seq reconciliation in >98% simulated reconnects.
- Tool idempotency honored when client_op_id is provided across reconnects in test harness.
- Console shows per-frame token attribution in sample workloads.

Open questions / risks:
- Frame retention window sizing vs. memory cost on server. Proposed: default 60s, configurable per-client tier. Need infra estimate.
- How to surface very large tool payloads (files, long documents) without bloating frames? Option: supply detachable blob URI from object-store with short-lived signed token.
- Compatibility with streaming SDKs in mobile ecosystems (swift/kotlin): need very small runtime for parsing frames.
- Security: tool metadata must not leak secrets; tool adapters should only accept whitelisted URIs.

Dependencies:
- Serving runtime: lightweight frame serializer and resume token logic (ENG-serving-runtime).
- Console: UI for per-frame telemetry and new trace spans (ENG-console-and-tooling / observability).
- SDKs: small parsing lib across languages (developer-experience).

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Product: finalize minimal frame schema (this doc) and ship formal spec RFC. (Owner: Asha)
- Eng: prototype server-side event framing + resume token (ENG-serving-runtime) - spike 5d (Ravi)
notes: This is an intentionally lightweight design to avoid locking into a heavy protocol.
We should run a small field test with 2 partners (one mobile app, one web dashboard).
Consider linking to prior streaming partial-commit experiments (DOC-1423).
